question: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 20 seconds. What is its speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** = Distance ÷ Time

Speed = 200 ÷ 20 = 10 m/s

To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Speed = 10 × 18/5 = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d8f631637ac8d69a3f778f555632b08d403fa746b5a3ad6f6cfd230b5ee22ab.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the train (Distance) = 200 m

Time taken to pass the pole = 20 s

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed (km/h) = Speed (m/s) × 18/5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 200 ÷ 20

⇒ Speed = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/h = 10 × 18/5

⇒ Speed = 2 × 18

⇒ Speed = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Rules

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed Concept

When two trains move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing a Platform or Bridge

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (like a platform), the total distance covered is the sum of the train length and the object length.</p
